basics.name: Mijin Goo
basics.label: Researcher
basics.summary:
I am a master's student in Construction Engineering at Seoul National University and a member of the SNU Construction Engineering & Management Lab (SNUCEM), under the supervision of Prof. Changbum Ryan Ahn. My research interests focus on data-driven construction management, particularly the use of artificial intelligence in architectural drawing review and construction safety.

My experience spans computer vision, GIS, and construction data, including work on fire detection systems, spatial data analysis, automated architectural drawing review, and soil–rock interface prediction. I aim to develop practical AI applications that support safer, more efficient, and better-informed construction processes.

projects.name: Development of a Drawing-Specialized Visual-Language Reasoning AI for Automated Design Review and 2D Plan Recognition of Multi-Family Housing
projects.summary: The goal of this project is to develop a visual-language reasoning AI technology specialized in architectural drawings in order to innovate the design document review process for multi-family housing, which is currently performed by human resources, into an AI-based automated review method. Through this project, we aim to significantly improve the efficiency and productivity of design document review tasks, while also enhancing the objectivity and reliability of review results through consistent application of review standards.

projects.name: Edge Keyframe Extraction-Driven VLM Testbed for Real-Time Construction Site Safety Monitoring
projects.summary: This project aims to build a real-time construction safety monitoring testbed that operates Vision-Language Models (VLMs) efficiently under resource-constrained edge computing environments. To address high false-alarm rates in deep learning models and computational latency in VLMs, we develop an edge-based keyframe extraction algorithm that selectively identifies risk-relevant frames based on activity energy. The selected keyframes are processed by a VLM agent for step-by-step hazard reasoning, with system latency and detection performance quantitatively validated at actual construction sites.
